report_name: Settra Ransomware Hits Retail, Manufacturing With RMM Tools

threat_actors.name: Settra
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group active since at least June 2026, targeting the retail and manufacturing sectors. The group uses the MeshAgent RMM tool for persistence, clears Windows Event Logs, disables the Windows Recovery Environment, and employs a 'Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver' (BYOVD) technique to disable security software. It operates a double extortion model with a data leak site.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware deployment and data exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Access Software
attack_patterns.description: The Settra group deployed the open-source RMM tool MeshAgent, masquerading as 'mvtcs.exe', to maintain persistent access to victim networks.

attack_patterns.name: Clear Windows Event Logs
attack_patterns.description: Settra operators used commands to clear critical Windows Event Logs, including Application, Security, Setup, and System, to hinder forensic analysis.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: The attackers disabled the Windows Recovery Environment using the command 'reagentc /disable' and attempted to delete recovery partitions to prevent system restoration.

attack_patterns.name: Disable or Modify Tools
attack_patterns.description: The Settra group utilized a Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) technique, using the legitimate but vulnerable Gigabyte driver 'gdrv.sys' to terminate security processes from the kernel.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The final Settra ransomware payload was deployed to encrypt files on victim systems as the primary means of impact and extortion.

malware.name: Settra Ransomware
malware.description: A ransomware variant used by the Settra group. The payload, often named after the victim's domain, encrypts files and is used in a double extortion scheme where data is also exfiltrated.

tools.name: MeshAgent
tools.description: An open-source Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tool deployed by the Settra group for persistent access. It was observed masquerading under the filename 'mvtcs.exe'.

tools.name: gdrv.sys
tools.description: A legitimate but vulnerable Gigabyte kernel driver used by the Settra group in a 'Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver' (BYOVD) attack to terminate security processes from the kernel level.

vulnerabilities.name: Vulnerable Gigabyte Driver (gdrv.sys)
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability in the legitimate Gigabyte kernel driver 'gdrv.sys' was abused by Settra operators in a BYOVD attack to gain kernel-level access and terminate security software.

identities.name: Retail Sector
identities.description: The retail sector is one of the primary targets of the Settra ransomware group.

identities.name: Manufacturing Sector
identities.description: The manufacturing sector is one of the primary targets of the Settra ransomware group.

infrastructure.name: Settra Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A data leak site used by the Settra ransomware group to publish stolen data as part of their double extortion strategy.

indicators.name: Settra Ransomware Associated Files
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Settra Ransomware Associated File Activity
id: 2a9b8c7d-6e5f-4d3c-b2a1-9f8e7d6c5b4a
status: experimental
description: Detects file or process creation events involving filenames associated with Settra ransomware TTPs, including a vulnerable Gigabyte driver and a renamed RMM tool.
references:
  - https://www.huntress.com/blog/new-settra-ransomware-variant
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-18
tags:
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.t1562.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\gdrv.sys'
      - '\mvtcs.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects files associated with Settra ransomware activity, including the vulnerable driver 'gdrv.sys' and the renamed MeshAgent RMM tool 'mvtcs.exe'.

indicators.name: Windows Recovery Environment Disabled via reagentc
indicators.pattern:
title: Windows Recovery Environment Disabled via reagentc
id: 3b8c7d6e-5f4d-4c3b-a2b1-8e7d6c5b4a9f
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of 'reagentc.exe' to disable the Windows Recovery Environment, a technique used by Settra ransomware to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.huntress.com/blog/new-settra-ransomware-variant
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-18
tags:
  - attack.t1490
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\reagentc.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: ' /disable'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects attempts to disable the Windows Recovery Environment using 'reagentc.exe', a technique used by Settra to inhibit system recovery.

indicators.name: Windows Security Event Log Cleared
indicators.pattern:
title: Windows Security Event Log Cleared
id: 4c7d6e5f-4d3c-4b2a-b1a9-f8e7d6c5b4a8
status: experimental
description: Detects the clearing of the Windows Security event log (Event ID 1102), a common defense evasion technique used by attackers like the Settra ransomware group.
references:
  - https://www.huntress.com/blog/new-settra-ransomware-variant
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-18
tags:
  - attack.t1070.001
level: high
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 1102
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the clearing of the Windows Security event log via Event ID 1102, a defense evasion tactic employed by Settra.
